newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products pressured by Russian export flows.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products pressured by Russian export flows.

text.p: Plentiful Russian material pressured Mediterranean oil products Thursday, traders said.
Gasoline was firm amid healthy demand out of Italy, a number of Eastern Med countries and north Africa. Premium unleaded was assessed at Med fob quotes +$2.50/+$4.50 or around $213/$216.

Naphtha was fairly balanced with pockets of demand amid a tightish market. There was talk of demand into Lavera and that a Spanish refinery also had a small requirement. Full-range cargo prices were assessed around $183/$188 cif NWE.

The market for 0.2 percent sulphur gas oil remained oversupplied with plentiful avails flowing from the Black Sea ports. Russian material was valued weaker at high cif quotes -$1.00-$1.50 basis Genoa, down from +$1.00 earlier in the week.

Some buying interest was seen for high sulphur gas oil and jet combo cargoes from West and South Africa, while the EN590 market was buoyed by demand from northern European buyers. A small Greek buying tender for EN590 closes on May 27.
Med fuel oil markets have become saturated by Russian material with the normal outlets not soaking it up.
"There is lots of Russian coming out both north and south and its putting high sulphur cracked under pressure because it is all coming out at cracked levels," said one trader.
As an indicator of poor demand an M-40 cargo that had sat outside Augusta for some days was put into tankage. Other cargoes were loading without destinations confirmed.
Buyers said low sulphur "was not exactly over-supplied" but the shortage was more than compensated by other grades. Russian supply was heard offered into Italy from as far as the Baltics.
But dealers said outright numbers were not yet coming off, although premiums have been eaten into.
